entries.title: Acts 17:1
segments: After passing through Amphipolis and Apollonia, Paul and Silas came to Thessalonica. Here the Jews had a Synagogue;

entries.title: Acts 17:2
segments: And, following his usual custom, Paul joined them, and for three Sabbaths addressed them, drawing his arguments from the Scriptures.

entries.title: Acts 17:3
segments: He laid before them and explained that the Christ must undergo suffering and rise from the dead; and "It is this man," he declared, "who is the Christ--this Jesus about whom I am telling you."

entries.title: Acts 17:4
segments: Some of the people were convinced, and threw in their lot with Paul and Silas, as did also a large body of Greeks who were accustomed to join in the Jewish services, and a great number of women belonging to the leading families.

entries.title: Acts 17:5
segments: But the Jews, becoming jealous, engaged some worthless fellows from the streets, and, getting a mob together, kept the city in an uproar. They attacked Jason's house, with the intention of bringing Paul and Silas before the Popular Assembly;

entries.title: Acts 17:6
segments: And, not finding them there, they proceeded to drag Jason and some of the Brethren before the City Magistrates, shouting out: "These men, who have turned the world upside down, have now come here,

entries.title: Acts 17:7
segments: And have been harbored by Jason! They say that some one else is king--a man called Jesus!"

entries.title: Acts 17:8
segments: On hearing this, the people and the City Magistrates were much concerned;

entries.title: Acts 17:9
segments: And, before letting them go, they took bail from Jason and the others.

entries.title: Acts 17:10
segments: That very night the Brethren sent Paul and Silas off to Beroea; and on reaching that place, they went to the Jewish Synagogue.

entries.title: Acts 17:11
segments: These Jews of Beroea were better disposed than those in Thessalonica, for they welcomed the Message with great readiness, and daily examined the Scriptures to see if what was said was true.

entries.title: Acts 17:12
segments: As a consequence, many of them became believers in Christ, besides a considerable number of Greek women of position, and of men also.

entries.title: Acts 17:13
segments: But, when the Jews of Thessalonica found out that God's Message had been delivered by Paul at Beroea, they came there too, exciting and disturbing the minds of the people.

entries.title: Acts 17:14
segments: Immediately upon that, the Brethren sent Paul off on his way to the sea coast, but both Silas and Timothy stayed behind in Beroea.

entries.title: Acts 17:15
segments: The friends who escorted Paul took him as far as Athens, and, after receiving a message for Silas and Timothy to join him as quickly as possible, they started on their return.

entries.title: Acts 17:16
segments: While Paul was waiting for them at Athens, his heart was stirred at seeing the whole city full of idols.

entries.title: Acts 17:17
segments: So he argued in the Synagogue with the Jews and with those who joined in their worship, as well as daily in the public Square with those who happened to be there.

entries.title: Acts 17:18
segments: Among others, some Epicurean and Stoic Philosophers joined issue with him. Some would ask "What is this prater wanting to make out?", while others would say "He seems to be a Preacher of foreign Deities." (This was because he was telling the Good News about Jesus and the Resurrection).

entries.title: Acts 17:19
segments: So they laid hold of him and took him to the Court of Areopagus. "May we hear," they asked, "what new teaching this is which you are giving?

entries.title: Acts 17:20
segments: For you are bringing some strange things to our notice, and we should like to know what they mean."

entries.title: Acts 17:21
segments: (All Athenians and the foreigners staying in the city found no time for anything else but telling, or listening to, the last new thing.)

entries.title: Acts 17:22
segments: So Paul took his stand in the middle of the Court, and said- -"Men of Athens, on every hand I see signs of your being very devout.

entries.title: Acts 17:23
segments: For as I was going about, looking at your sacred shrines, I came upon an altar with this inscription--'To an Unknown God.' What, therefore, you worship in ignorance, that I am now proclaiming to you.

entries.title: Acts 17:24
segments: The God who made the world and all things that are in it-- he, Lord as he is of Heaven and Earth, does not dwell in temples made by hands,

entries.title: Acts 17:25
segments: Nor yet do human hands minister to his wants, as though he needed anything, since he himself gives, to all, life, and breath, and all things.

entries.title: Acts 17:26
segments: He made all races of the earth's surface--fixing a time for their rise and fall, and the limits of their settlements--

entries.title: Acts 17:27
segments: That they might search for God, if by any means they might feel their way to him and find him. And yet he is not really far from any one of us;

entries.title: Acts 17:28
segments: For in him we live and move and are. To use the words of some of your own poets--'His offspring, too, are we.'

entries.title: Acts 17:29
segments: Therefore, as the offspring of God, we must not think that the Deity has any resemblance to anything made of gold, or silver, or stone--a work of human art and imagination.

entries.title: Acts 17:30
segments: True, God looked with indulgence on the days of men's ignorance, but now he is announcing to every one everywhere the need for repentance,

entries.title: Acts 17:31
segments: Because he has fixed a day on which he intends to 'judge the world with justice,' by a man whom he has appointed--and of this he has given all men a pledge by raising this man from the dead."

entries.title: Acts 17:32
segments: On hearing of a resurrection of the dead, some began jeering, but others said that they would hear what he had to say about that another time.

entries.title: Acts 17:33
segments: And so Paul left the Court.

entries.title: Acts 17:34
segments: There were, however, some men who joined him, and became believers in Christ. Among them were Dionysius, a member of the Court of Areopagus, a woman named Damaris, and several others.
